creators.name: Zimoun
creators.bio: Swiss artist who builds large architectural installations from hundreds of identical cheap parts (dc-motors, cotton balls, cardboard boxes, wires, sticks) whose collective rattling becomes a dense, living sound field; each title simply lists its materials.
creators.why: He shows how a crowd of tiny identical agents, each doing one dumb thing, turns a whole room into an organism you can hear and walk through.
creators.role_zh: 声音雕塑家、装置艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士艺术家，用成百上千个廉价而相同的零件（直流电机、棉球、纸箱、铁丝、木棍）搭建建筑尺度的装置，它们集体的敲击声汇成一片密集而有生命感的声场；作品标题就是材料清单。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了：一大群只会做一件简单事情的小单元，就能把整个房间变成一个可以听、可以走进去的有机体。

creators.name: Reuben Margolin
creators.bio: American kinetic sculptor who builds hanging wave sculptures from wood, strings, pulleys, bicycle wheels and glass, in which camshafts add sine waves together so that thousands of points ripple like water or a caterpillar's back.
creators.why: His pieces make the math of waves physically visible, a direct lesson for anyone animating many points in space from a few driving functions.
creators.role_zh: 动态雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 美国动态雕塑家，用木头、绳子、滑轮、自行车轮和玻璃搭建悬挂式波浪雕塑：凸轮轴把几条正弦波叠加起来，让成千上万个点像水面或毛毛虫的背一样起伏。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品把波的数学变成看得见的实物，对任何想用几个驱动函数让空间中大量点运动起来的人都是直接的一课。

creators.name: Ned Kahn
creators.bio: American artist, trained at the Exploratorium, whose façades and sculptures are skins of thousands of hinged aluminium or plastic panels, fog vortices and moving sand that reveal wind, water and light as they pass through.
creators.why: He treats buildings as sensors: his wind veils turn an invisible force into a moving image across a whole façade, with no electronics at all.
creators.role_zh: 环境艺术家、雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，出身于旧金山探索馆（Exploratorium）。他的建筑立面和雕塑由成千上万块铰接的铝片或塑料片、雾气漩涡和流动的沙构成，让风、水和光经过时显形。
creators.why_zh: 他把建筑当成传感器：风幕把看不见的力变成整面墙上流动的影像，而且完全不用电子元件。
creators.based_zh: 美国加州塞巴斯托波尔

creators.name: Anthony Howe
creators.bio: American sculptor who machines large stainless-steel wind sculptures whose hundreds of cups and blades rotate into shimmering, hypnotic 3D patterns; he designed the kinetic cauldron sculpture for the Rio 2016 Olympic Games.
creators.why: His sculptures show how nested rotations turn one input (wind) into an endlessly changing volumetric form, a model for procedural motion in AR.
creators.role_zh: 风动雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家，用数控加工的不锈钢制作大型风动雕塑，数百个杯片和叶片旋转出闪烁、令人着迷的三维图案；他设计了 2016 年里约奥运会的动态火炬台雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他的雕塑说明，嵌套的旋转可以把单一输入（风）变成不断变化的立体形态，是 AR 程序化运动的好范本。
creators.based_zh: 美国华盛顿州奥卡斯岛

creators.name: Arthur Ganson
creators.bio: American sculptor whose small hand-built machines of wire and gears perform poetic gestures: a wishbone that walks, a chair that explodes and reassembles, a gear train that ends in concrete; many are on long-term view at the MIT Museum.
creators.why: Ganson proves that a single, well-timed gesture of an ordinary object can carry more emotion than any spectacle, a core lesson for small AR interventions.
creators.role_zh: 动态雕塑家、工程师
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家，用铁丝和齿轮亲手制作小型机器，让它们完成富有诗意的动作：会走路的许愿骨、会炸开又重新拼合的椅子、最后一个齿轮被浇进混凝土的齿轮组；许多作品长期陈列于 MIT 博物馆。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了普通物件一个时机恰当的动作，比任何大场面都更能打动人，这是做小型 AR 介入的核心一课。
creators.based_zh: 美国马萨诸塞州萨默维尔

creators.name: Ralfonso
creators.bio: Swiss-born artist Ralf Alfonso (Ralfonso) creates wind-driven stainless-steel kinetic sculptures, light sculptures and interactive murals for public spaces worldwide, and co-founded the Kinetic Art Organization (KAO).
creators.why: His public wind-and-light pieces show how a sculpture can change character from day to night and with the weather, as an AR layer should.
creators.role_zh: 动态、光与互动雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士出生的艺术家 Ralf Alfonso（Ralfonso）为世界各地的公共空间制作风动不锈钢动态雕塑、光雕塑和互动壁画，并参与创立了动态艺术组织 Kinetic Art Organization（KAO）。
creators.why_zh: 他的风与光公共雕塑会随昼夜和天气变换性格，这正是 AR 图层应有的样子。

creators.name: Jennifer Townley
creators.bio: Dutch artist who designs precise mechanical sculptures of gears, spirals and repeated parts whose slightly different rotation speeds produce slowly shifting, hypnotic patterns, as well as drawing machines.
creators.why: Her work shows how two nearly identical rhythms drifting out of phase create endless variation, a cheap and elegant engine for generative AR motion.
creators.role_zh: 机械雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰艺术家，用齿轮、螺旋和重复部件设计精密的机械雕塑，各部件转速略有不同，产生缓慢变化、令人着迷的图案；她也制作绘图机器。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品说明，两个几乎相同的节奏彼此错相，就能生成无穷的变化，是 AR 生成式运动便宜又优雅的引擎。

creators.name: Bruce Shapiro
creators.bio: American artist and engineer who has built computer-controlled kinetic sculptures since the 1990s; his Sisyphus tables use a hidden magnet to roll a steel ball through sand, drawing and erasing patterns forever.
creators.why: Sisyphus is the purest example of a trace: a single moving point whose path becomes the artwork and then disappears.
creators.role_zh: 动态艺术家、运动控制工程师
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家兼工程师，自 1990 年代起制作计算机控制的动态雕塑；他的 Sisyphus 沙桌用隐藏磁铁推动钢珠在沙中滚动，永无止境地画出又抹去图案。
creators.why_zh: Sisyphus 是“痕迹”最纯粹的例子：一个移动的点，它的路径就是作品，随后又消失。

creators.name: John Edmark
creators.bio: American artist and Stanford design lecturer who 3D-prints sculptures built on the golden angle; spun under a strobe light, his Blooms appear to unfold endlessly like living flowers.
creators.why: Edmark shows that the right geometry plus a synchronised flash turns a static object into animation, the same trick as frame-synced AR rendering.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、发明家、设计讲师
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，斯坦福大学设计讲师，用 3D 打印制作基于黄金角的雕塑；在频闪灯下旋转时，他的 Blooms 仿佛花朵在无限绽放。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了恰当的几何加上同步闪光，就能把静物变成动画，这与 AR 按帧同步渲染是同一个把戏。

creators.name: Akinori Goto
creators.bio: Japanese media artist who creates 3D-printed zoetropes: a spinning lattice of frozen figures lit by a thin projected line of light, so that a walking or dancing body appears to move inside the object.
creators.why: His toki- works show that light can select which slice of a physical object we see, letting a fixed form hold a whole animation.
creators.role_zh: 媒体艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 日本媒体艺术家，制作 3D 打印的走马灯（zoetrope）：一个由凝固人形组成的网格旋转，被一道细细的投影光线照亮，于是行走或舞蹈的身体仿佛在物体内部动了起来。
creators.why_zh: 他的 toki- 系列说明，光可以挑选我们看见物体的哪一个切片，让一个固定的形体容纳一整段动画。

creators.name: Gregory Barsamian
creators.bio: American sculptor who since the 1980s has built large 3D zoetropes: dozens of sculpted objects spin on armatures while a synchronised strobe fuses them into dreamlike, morphing animations in physical space.
creators.why: Barsamian's rooms are animation without a screen, showing how motion can be embedded in real matter and revealed only by light timing.
creators.role_zh: 频闪立体动画雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家，自 1980 年代起制作大型立体走马灯：几十个雕塑件在支架上旋转，同步频闪灯把它们融合成在真实空间里变形的梦境动画。
creators.why_zh: 他的展厅是没有屏幕的动画，说明运动可以嵌进真实物质里，只靠光的时序显现出来。

creators.name: Toshio Iwai (岩井俊雄)
creators.bio: Japanese media artist whose early Time Stratum zoetropes used the flicker of TV monitors as a strobe; he later created Morphovision with NHK, the piano performance with Ryuichi Sakamoto, Electroplankton and the Tenori-on instrument.
creators.why: Iwai connects pre-cinema optical toys with interactive media, showing AR designers that timing light against motion is itself a display technology.
creators.role_zh: 媒体艺术家、游戏设计师
creators.bio_zh: 日本媒体艺术家，早期的 Time Stratum（时间层）系列走马灯用电视显示器的闪烁充当频闪；后来与 NHK 合作 Morphovision，与坂本龙一合作钢琴演出，并创作了 Electroplankton 和 Tenori-on 乐器。
creators.why_zh: 他把电影诞生前的光学玩具与互动媒体连在一起，告诉 AR 设计者：让光的时序与运动对齐，本身就是一种显示技术。

creators.name: ART+COM Studios (Joachim Sauter)
creators.role: Berlin design studio for kinetic sculpture and media installations
creators.bio: Founded in 1988 by Joachim Sauter and others, ART+COM builds kinetic sculptures such as Kinetic Rain and the BMW Museum's Kinetic Sculpture, where hundreds of motor-driven elements draw shapes in the air.
creators.why: Their sculptures show how many small synchronized elements can form one shape in space, which is exactly how particle and voxel effects work in AR.
creators.role_zh: 柏林的动态雕塑与媒体装置设计工作室
creators.bio_zh: 由 Joachim Sauter 等人于 1988 年创立，代表作包括樟宜机场的 Kinetic Rain 和宝马博物馆的 Kinetic Sculpture：数百个由电机驱动的元素在空中拼出形状。
creators.why_zh: 他们的雕塑展示了大量小元素同步运动如何在空间中组成一个整体形状，这正是 AR 中粒子与体素效果的原理。

creators.name: Christopher Bauder / WHITEvoid
creators.role: Light and kinetic artist; founder of WHITEvoid and the Kinetic Lights system
creators.bio: Berlin artist whose studio WHITEvoid makes kinetic light installations and audiovisual shows, often with Robert Henke (Atom, GRID, DEEP WEB) and Kangding Ray (SKALAR), and who marked the Berlin Wall with 8,000 glowing balloons in Lichtgrenze.
creators.why: He choreographs light in 3D space with winches, spheres and mirrors, the physical version of animating virtual objects in a room.
creators.role_zh: 光与动态艺术家；WHITEvoid 工作室与 Kinetic Lights 系统创始人
creators.bio_zh: 柏林艺术家，其工作室 WHITEvoid 制作动态灯光装置与视听演出，常与 Robert Henke（Atom、GRID、DEEP WEB）和 Kangding Ray（SKALAR）合作；他还用 8000 个发光气球在 Lichtgrenze 中重现了柏林墙的走向。
creators.why_zh: 他用绞盘、光球和镜面在三维空间里编排光，这就是在房间里给虚拟物体做动画的实体版本。

creators.name: Troika (Eva Rucki, Conny Freyer & Sebastien Noel)
creators.role: London art collective working with perception, light and kinetic sculpture
creators.bio: Troika is a London collective founded in 2003 whose sculptures and installations, from the flip-dot Cloud at Heathrow to the rotating Dark Matter, play with perception, light and the gap between what we see and what we know.
creators.why: Their works make a viewer's position and movement part of the image, a core lesson for any AR piece that changes as you walk around it.
creators.role_zh: 关注感知、光与动态雕塑的伦敦艺术团体
creators.bio_zh: Troika 于 2003 年在伦敦成立，作品从希思罗机场的翻片装置 Cloud 到旋转雕塑 Dark Matter，都在玩弄感知与光，探讨我们看到的与我们知道的之间的落差。
creators.why_zh: 他们让观众的位置和移动成为图像的一部分，这正是任何“绕着走会变”的 AR 作品的核心课题。

creators.name: United Visual Artists (UVA)
creators.role: London art practice for light, sound and responsive installations
creators.bio: Founded by Matt Clark in 2003 after building stage visuals for Massive Attack, UVA makes installations such as Volume, Momentum and Our Time that use light, pendulums and sound to change how people feel space and time.
creators.why: UVA treats light as something you walk through and that answers your presence, the same design space as room-scale AR.
creators.role_zh: 以光、声音和互动装置为媒介的伦敦艺术团体
creators.bio_zh: 由 Matt Clark 于 2003 年创立，起步于为 Massive Attack 制作舞台视觉；代表作 Volume、Momentum 和 Our Time 用光、摆锤和声音改变人们对空间与时间的感受。
creators.why_zh: UVA 把光当作可以穿行其中、并会回应你存在的东西，这与房间尺度的 AR 是同一个设计空间。

creators.name: Studio Swine / A.A. Murakami (Azusa Murakami & Alexander Groves)
creators.role: Art and design duo making ephemeral sculptures from mist, bubbles and light
creators.bio: Japanese-British duo Azusa Murakami and Alexander Groves, who worked as Studio Swine and now as A.A. Murakami, build machines that make fleeting forms, such as mist-filled bubbles that bloom from a tree and burst on your hand.
creators.why: They design objects that exist for a few seconds, a strong model for AR content that appears, lives briefly and disappears.
creators.role_zh: 用雾、泡泡和光制作转瞬即逝雕塑的艺术设计二人组
creators.bio_zh: 日英二人组 Azusa Murakami 与 Alexander Groves，曾以 Studio Swine 为名，现以 A.A. Murakami 创作；他们制造会生成短暂形态的机器，比如从树上绽放、落在手上才破裂的雾气泡泡。
creators.why_zh: 他们设计只存在几秒钟的物体，这是 AR 内容“出现、短暂存在、消失”的极好范例。

creators.name: Conrad Shawcross
creators.role: Sculptor of machines, robots and light
creators.bio: British sculptor (born 1977, Royal Academician) whose mechanical sculptures, from Slow Arc Inside a Cube to the robot of The ADA Project, trace geometry, time and motion with a moving light or arm.
creators.why: His machines turn a single moving point into a whole architecture of shadow and light, a lesson in how simple motion creates volume.
creators.role_zh: 以机器、机械臂和光为材料的雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 英国雕塑家（1977 年生，英国皇家艺术研究院院士），作品从 Slow Arc Inside a Cube 到 The ADA Project 的机械臂，用移动的光点或手臂描绘几何、时间与运动。
creators.why_zh: 他的机器让一个移动的点变成一整座光影建筑，说明简单的运动也能生成体积。

creators.name: Shinji Ohmaki (大巻伸嗣)
creators.role: Installation artist working with air, fabric, bubbles and light
creators.bio: Japanese artist (born 1971) who fills spaces with slowly floating fabric (Liminal Air Space-Time), streams of soap bubbles (Memorial Rebirth) and rotating lights, making air and time visible.
creators.why: He makes the invisible medium of a room, the air, into the artwork, a model for AR effects that visualize wind, breath or presence.
creators.role_zh: 以空气、布料、泡泡和光为材料的装置艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家大巻伸嗣（1971 年生），用缓慢漂浮的巨大布料（Liminal Air Space-Time）、如潮水般的肥皂泡（Memorial Rebirth）和旋转灯光填满空间，让空气与时间变得可见。
creators.why_zh: 他把房间里看不见的介质——空气——变成作品本身，为可视化风、呼吸或存在感的 AR 效果提供了范例。

creators.name: Humans since 1982 (Per Emanuelsson & Bastian Bischoff)
creators.role: Swedish-German art studio for kinetic clock installations
creators.bio: Studio founded in 2008 by Per Emanuelsson and Bastian Bischoff, known for ClockClock and A Million Times: grids of analogue clock hands that dance in unison and then settle to spell the current time.
creators.why: They turn hundreds of identical parts into a choreographed display, showing how a grid of simple rotating elements can carry both motion and information.
creators.role_zh: 制作动态时钟装置的瑞典-德国艺术工作室
creators.bio_zh: 由 Per Emanuelsson 与 Bastian Bischoff 于 2008 年创立，以 ClockClock 和 A Million Times 闻名：成百上千根模拟时钟指针整齐起舞，最后停下来拼出当前时间。
creators.why_zh: 他们把成百个相同的部件变成一场编排好的表演，说明一组简单的旋转元素既能表现运动，也能传达信息。

creators.name: Maarten Baas
creators.role: Dutch designer; author of the Real Time clock series
creators.bio: Dutch designer (born 1978) whose Real Time series films people drawing, sweeping or painting the hands of a clock in real time for twelve hours, turning a clock face into a performance.
creators.why: Real Time shows that a hidden human performance, played back in sync with the world, can replace a machine interface, a trick AR can use with recorded volumetric performers.
creators.role_zh: 荷兰设计师；Real Time 时钟系列作者
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰设计师 Maarten Baas（1978 年生），其 Real Time 系列拍摄真人连续 12 小时实时画出、扫出或涂出时钟指针，把钟面变成一场表演。
creators.why_zh: Real Time 说明，一段与现实时间同步播放的真人表演可以取代机械界面，AR 用录制的体积人像时也能用上这一招。

creators.name: Jonpasang (전파상)
creators.bio: Seoul collective of media artists and engineers that builds large kinetic works, best known for Hyper-Matrix, the moving cube wall of the Hyundai Motor Group Pavilion at Expo 2012 Yeosu.
creators.why: Hyper-Matrix proves that a wall of physical pixels can move like a screen, a reference for AR that pushes surfaces in and out of real architecture.
creators.role_zh: 首尔媒体艺术团体
creators.bio_zh: 首尔的媒体艺术家与工程师团体（전파상），擅长大型动态装置，代表作是 2012 年丽水世博会现代汽车集团馆的动态方块墙 Hyper-Matrix。
creators.why_zh: Hyper-Matrix 证明一面由实体像素组成的墙也能像屏幕一样运动，是 AR 让真实建筑表面起伏变形的参考。

creators.name: BREAKFAST (Andrew Zolty)
creators.role: Brooklyn studio for kinetic, data-driven flip-disc and Brixel artworks
creators.bio: Studio founded by Andrew Zolty that invents kinetic media such as flip-discs and rotating Brixels, making walls that mirror passers-by or visualize live wind, weather and ocean data.
creators.why: BREAKFAST shows how a physical display can react to bodies and live data at the same time, the two inputs most AR pieces also combine.
creators.role_zh: 制作翻片（flip-disc）与 Brixel 动态、数据驱动艺术的布鲁克林工作室
creators.bio_zh: 由 Andrew Zolty 创立，发明了翻片、可旋转的 Brixel 等动态媒介，做出能映照路人、或实时呈现风、天气与海洋数据的墙面。
creators.why_zh: BREAKFAST 展示了一块实体显示面如何同时回应身体与实时数据，而这两种输入也是很多 AR 作品会组合使用的。

creators.name: Nils Völker
creators.role: Berlin artist making kinetic installations from inflatable bags
creators.bio: German artist (born 1979) who builds large grids of plastic bags that inflate and deflate in computed waves, and machines that draw light patterns.
creators.why: He makes breathing, wave-like motion out of the cheapest material, proof that timing matters more than rendering fidelity.
creators.role_zh: 用充气塑料袋制作动态装置的柏林艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家 Nils Völker（1979 年生），用成片的塑料袋按计算好的波形充气、放气，也制作画光的绘图机器。
creators.why_zh: 他用最廉价的材料做出会呼吸般的波动，证明节奏比渲染精度更重要。

creators.name: Daniel Palacios
creators.bio: Spanish artist who builds machines that make invisible processes visible: a spinning rope that turns the movement of visitors into waves and sound, and a laser that engraves growth rings as they happen.
creators.why: His Waves shows how a single line can become a living, readable response to a crowd.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；动态与声音装置
creators.bio_zh: 西班牙艺术家，擅长制造让看不见的过程显形的机器：一根旋转的绳子把观众的动作变成波浪和声音，一束激光把树木年轮的生长实时刻出来。
creators.why_zh: 他的《Waves》说明一根线就能变成对人群的鲜活、可读的回应。

creators.name: David Bowen
creators.role: Artist; professor at the University of Minnesota Duluth
creators.bio: American artist who connects robotic devices to natural systems — wind, waves, clouds, houseflies, plants — so that remote or invisible forces drive machines in the gallery.
creators.why: He treats live sensor data from nature as a puppeteer, the same pattern AR uses when it lets real-world signals move virtual things.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；明尼苏达大学德卢斯分校教授
creators.based_zh: 德卢斯，美国明尼苏达州
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，把机器人装置接到自然系统上——风、浪、云、苍蝇、植物——让远方或看不见的力量在展厅里驱动机器。
creators.why_zh: 他把来自自然的实时传感数据当作操偶师，这正是 AR 用真实世界信号驱动虚拟物体的思路。

creators.name: Julius Popp
creators.bio: German artist best known for bit.fall, a waterfall whose drops are released by computer-controlled valves to write words taken live from news feeds.
creators.why: bit.fall turns falling water into a display that exists for one second — information made physical and temporary.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；动态信息雕塑
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家，最知名的作品是《bit.fall》：由电脑控制的阀门放出水滴，在下落的水帘中写出实时抓取的新闻词语。
creators.why_zh: 《bit.fall》把下落的水变成只存在一秒的显示屏——信息被物质化，而且转瞬即逝。

creators.name: Jason Bruges Studio
creators.bio: London studio founded by Jason Bruges in 2001 that makes responsive light, kinetic and robotic installations for public spaces, hospitals and architecture.
creators.why: Their pieces treat buildings and corridors as sensing surfaces that notice passers-by and answer with light.
creators.role_zh: 互动艺术与建筑工作室
creators.bio_zh: Jason Bruges 于 2001 年在伦敦创立的工作室，为公共空间、医院和建筑制作会回应人的灯光、动态和机器人装置。
creators.why_zh: 他们把建筑和走廊当作会感知的表面，注意到路人并用光来回应。

creators.name: Philip Beesley / Living Architecture Systems Group
creators.role: Architect and artist; professor at the University of Waterloo
creators.bio: Canadian architect whose 'living architecture' installations are dense canopies of acrylic fronds, sensors, shape-memory actuators, lights and chemistry that breathe and ripple as visitors move through them.
creators.why: He shows how a whole room can feel alive when thousands of small elements react locally to a body nearby.
creators.role_zh: 建筑师、艺术家；滑铁卢大学教授
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大建筑师，他的“活的建筑”装置由亚克力叶片、传感器、形状记忆合金、灯光和化学组件密集编织成穹顶，观众经过时它会呼吸、起伏。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了当成千上万个小单元各自对附近的身体做出反应时，整个房间会显得有生命。

creators.name: Behnaz Farahi
creators.role: Designer and artist; interactive wearables and responsive architecture
creators.bio: Iranian-born designer who makes 3D-printed garments and kinetic surfaces that react to gaze, facial expression, speech and brain activity using cameras, soft robotics and shape-memory alloys.
creators.why: Her garments make the social signals between people visible on the body — a physical version of a face-tracking AR filter.
creators.role_zh: 设计师、艺术家；互动可穿戴与响应式建筑
creators.bio_zh: 出生于伊朗的设计师，用摄像头、软体机器人和形状记忆合金制作 3D 打印服装与动态表面，能对目光、表情、语音和脑电活动做出反应。
creators.why_zh: 她的服装把人与人之间的社交信号显现在身体上——相当于一个实体版的人脸追踪 AR 滤镜。

creators.name: Antonin Fourneau
creators.bio: French artist who makes playful public installations and arcade machines; his Water Light Graffiti wall lights up wherever it is touched with water.
creators.why: He found a way to paint with light using nothing but a wet brush — drawing that leaves no trace.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、游戏设计师
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，制作好玩的公共装置和街机；他的《Water Light Graffiti》墙面只要被水碰到就会亮起来。
creators.why_zh: 他找到了一种只用湿刷子就能用光作画的方法——画了不留痕迹。

creators.name: David Rokeby
creators.role: Artist; pioneer of interactive sound and vision installations
creators.bio: Canadian artist who since the early 1980s has built camera-based systems that answer body movement with sound (Very Nervous System) or look at objects and speak about them (The Giver of Names).
creators.why: Very Nervous System is one of the first works where the whole body in an empty room became the interface.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；互动声音与视觉装置先驱
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大艺术家，自 1980 年代初开始用摄像头搭建系统：用声音回应身体动作（《Very Nervous System》），或观看物体并说出关于它的句子（《The Giver of Names》）。
creators.why_zh: 《Very Nervous System》是最早把空房间里的整个身体变成界面的作品之一。

creators.name: Chico MacMurtrie / Amorphic Robot Works
creators.bio: American artist who leads Amorphic Robot Works, a collective building pneumatic robots and giant inflatable sculptures that breathe, unfold and move like bodies.
creators.why: His inflatables show how soft, breathing forms can make architecture feel like a creature.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；机器人与充气雕塑
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，领导 Amorphic Robot Works 团队，制作会像身体一样呼吸、展开和移动的气动机器人与巨型充气雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他的充气作品说明柔软、会呼吸的形体能让建筑像生物一样。

creators.name: dECOi / Mark Goulthorpe (HypoSurface)
creators.bio: dECOi is the architecture practice of Mark Goulthorpe; with MIT they developed HypoSurface, a wall of hundreds of pneumatically driven metal plates that ripples into waves, patterns and letters in response to sound and movement.
creators.why: HypoSurface is an early full-size 'shape display' — a wall that moves like a screen.
creators.role_zh: 建筑事务所；动态表面研究
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 剑桥，美国
creators.bio_zh: dECOi 是 Mark Goulthorpe 的建筑事务所，与 MIT 合作开发了 HypoSurface：由数百块气动金属片组成的墙，能根据声音和动作起伏成波浪、图案和文字。
creators.why_zh: HypoSurface 是早期的真人尺度“形状显示器”——一面像屏幕一样会动的墙。

creators.name: Aaron Sherwood
creators.bio: American media artist and composer (Purring Tiger, with Kiori Kawai) who builds interactive audiovisual installations and performances, including Firewall, a stretched spandex membrane that reacts to touch.
creators.why: Firewall turns a soft fabric into a depth-sensing interface people want to push their hands into.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、作曲家、创意技术人
creators.bio_zh: 美国媒体艺术家和作曲家（与 Kiori Kawai 组成 Purring Tiger），制作互动视听装置与演出，代表作《Firewall》是一张会对按压做出反应的弹力布幕。
creators.why_zh: 《Firewall》把一块柔软的布变成人们忍不住想把手按进去的深度感应界面。

creators.name: Rebecca Horn
creators.role: Artist; performance, body extensions and kinetic sculpture
creators.bio: German artist (1944–2024) who began with wearable 'body extensions' that stretched the senses and moved on to feathered, motorised sculptures and room-sized machines that seem to breathe, paint and play.
creators.why: She treated the body as an interface to be extended and the machine as a performer, which is exactly the space where wearable AR lives.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；表演、身体延伸装置与动态雕塑
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家（1944–2024），早期以可穿戴的“身体延伸”作品拓展感官，后来创作带羽毛的电动雕塑和能“呼吸”、绘画、演奏的房间尺度机器。
creators.why_zh: 她把身体当作可以延伸的界面、把机器当作表演者，这正是可穿戴 AR 所处的空间。
creators.based_zh: 柏林，德国 / 巴黎，法国

creators.name: Jesús Rafael Soto
creators.role: Artist; kinetic and op art pioneer
creators.bio: Venezuelan artist (1923–2005) of the Paris kinetic movement, known for 'Vibrations' that shimmer as you move and for 'Penetrables', rooms of hanging threads or tubes that visitors walk through.
creators.why: His works only exist through the viewer's motion and body, a direct lesson for parallax, occlusion and walk-through volumes in AR.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；动态艺术与欧普艺术先驱
creators.bio_zh: 委内瑞拉艺术家（1923–2005），巴黎动态艺术运动的核心人物，以随观者移动而颤动的“振动”系列和可以走进去的悬挂线管空间“可穿透体”（Penetrables）闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品只有在观者移动、身体进入时才成立，对 AR 中的视差、遮挡和可穿行体积是直接的启发。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 加拉加斯，委内瑞拉

creators.name: Julio Le Parc
creators.role: Artist; light and kinetic art, co-founder of GRAV
creators.bio: Argentine artist (born 1928) and co-founder of GRAV (Groupe de Recherche d'Art Visuel), who since the late 1950s has built mobiles of reflective plates, moving-light rooms and games that turn spectators into participants.
creators.why: He made light itself move through space and insisted the viewer complete the work, two principles at the heart of AR design.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；光与动态艺术，GRAV 视觉艺术研究小组联合创始人
creators.bio_zh: 阿根廷艺术家（生于 1928 年），GRAV（视觉艺术研究小组）联合创始人。自 1950 年代末起创作反光片组成的“连续运动”装置、流动光影房间和让观众参与的游戏。
creators.why_zh: 他让光本身在空间里流动，并坚持由观众完成作品，这两点正是 AR 设计的核心。

creators.name: Carlos Cruz-Diez
creators.role: Artist; researcher of colour as an event
creators.bio: Venezuelan artist (1923–2019) who treated colour as something that happens in real time and space, through series such as Physichromie, Transchromie, Chromointerference and the walk-in colour rooms of Chromosaturation.
creators.why: He showed that colour can change with the viewer's position and time, which is a model for view-dependent materials and colour overlays in AR.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；把色彩当作“事件”来研究
creators.bio_zh: 委内瑞拉艺术家（1923–2019），把色彩视为在时间和空间中实时发生的现象，代表系列包括 Physichromie、Transchromie、Chromointerference，以及可以走进去的色彩房间 Chromosaturation。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了颜色会随观者位置和时间而变化，这是 AR 中视角相关材质与色彩叠加的范本。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 加拉加斯，委内瑞拉

creators.name: Otto Piene
creators.role: Artist; co-founder of ZERO, pioneer of light and sky art
creators.bio: German artist (1928–2014), co-founder of the ZERO group and later director of MIT's Center for Advanced Visual Studies, who made rotating perforated lamps flood rooms with moving light ('Lichtballett') and later inflatable sky sculptures.
creators.why: His light ballets turn a whole room into a moving display using only a lamp and a perforated shell, a lesson in cheap, spatial light effects.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；ZERO 小组联合创始人，光艺术与天空艺术先驱
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家（1928–2014），ZERO 小组联合创始人，后任 MIT 高级视觉研究中心主任。他用旋转的穿孔灯让整个房间充满流动的光点（“光之芭蕾”），后来又创作充气天空雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他的光之芭蕾只用一盏灯和一个穿孔外壳就把整个房间变成运动的屏幕，是低成本空间光效的范例。
creators.based_zh: 杜塞尔多夫，德国 / 剑桥，美国

creators.name: Nam June Paik (白南准)
creators.based: New York, US / Seoul, South Korea
creators.bio: Korean-American artist (1932–2006) of Fluxus who turned television into a sculptural, playable material: magnets bending the picture, TVs growing in a garden, a Buddha watching himself on a closed circuit, robots and TV cellos in performance.
creators.why: He was the first to treat the screen as a physical object in space that the audience can touch and distort, the conceptual root of screen-in-the-world AR.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；录像艺术之父
creators.bio_zh: 韩裔美国艺术家（1932–2006），激浪派成员，把电视变成可雕塑、可玩的材料：用磁铁扭曲画面、让电视在花园里生长、让佛像在闭路电视里看自己，还有机器人和电视大提琴表演。
creators.why_zh: 他最早把屏幕当作空间中的物体，让观众可以触碰和扭曲它，这是“屏幕进入现实世界”式 AR 的概念源头。
creators.based_zh: 纽约，美国 / 首尔，韩国

creators.name: Nicolas Schöffer
creators.bio: Hungarian-born French artist (1912–1992) who built 'spatiodynamic' sculptures of polished metal, motors and light, including CYSP 1 (1956), the first sculpture to react autonomously to sound, light and movement, and a 52 m cybernetic light tower in Liège.
creators.why: He was the first to give a sculpture sensors and behaviour, the same loop of sensing and responding that drives interactive AR content.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；控制论艺术之父
creators.bio_zh: 匈牙利裔法国艺术家（1912–1992），用抛光金属、电机和灯光制作“空间动力”雕塑。1956 年的 CYSP 1 是第一件能自主响应声音、光和运动的雕塑，他还在列日建造了 52 米高的控制论光塔。
creators.why_zh: 他最早给雕塑装上传感器和行为逻辑，这正是驱动交互式 AR 内容的“感知—回应”循环。

creators.name: Edward Ihnatowicz
creators.role: Artist; pioneer of robotic and cybernetic sculpture
creators.bio: Polish-born British sculptor (1926–1988) whose Senster (1970), a 4 m hydraulic creature at Philips' Evoluon, turned toward quiet sounds and slow movement, and whose SAM (1968) leaned toward voices at Cybernetic Serendipity.
creators.why: He proved that a few sensors and simple rules can give an object a believable personality, a key idea for AR characters that notice people.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；机器人与控制论雕塑先驱
creators.bio_zh: 波兰裔英国雕塑家（1926–1988）。他的 Senster（1970）是陈列在飞利浦 Evoluon 的 4 米液压“生物”，会转向轻柔的声音和缓慢的动作；SAM（1968）则在“控制论的偶然”展上向说话的人探身。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了几个传感器加简单规则就能让物体拥有可信的个性，这是会“注意到人”的 AR 角色的关键思路。

creators.name: Jean Tinguely
creators.role: Artist; maker of absurd kinetic machines
creators.bio: Swiss artist (1925–1991) who built noisy, self-destroying and drawing machines from scrap, from the Méta-Matic drawing robots (1959) and Homage to New York (1960) to the forest giant Le Cyclop.
creators.why: His machines make process, noise and failure the spectacle, a reminder that visible mechanics and chance can be more engaging than polish.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；荒诞动态机器的制造者
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士艺术家（1925–1991），用废旧零件制造吵闹、会自毁、会画画的机器，从 Méta-Matic 绘画机器（1959）、《向纽约致敬》（1960）到森林中的巨型雕塑 Le Cyclop。
creators.why_zh: 他的机器把过程、噪音和失败本身变成奇观，提醒我们：可见的机制与偶然性往往比精致更吸引人。
creators.based_zh: 巴塞尔，瑞士 / 巴黎，法国

creators.name: Alexander Calder
creators.bio: American sculptor (1898–1976) who invented the mobile, balanced abstract shapes that move with air and touch, and who performed his wire Cirque Calder by hand.
creators.why: His mobiles show how a few balanced parts can create endless motion, a model for physics-driven, ambient AR objects.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；“动态雕塑”（mobile）的发明者
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家（1898–1976），发明了随空气与触碰而运动的平衡抽象雕塑“mobile”，还亲手表演铁丝马戏团 Cirque Calder。
creators.why_zh: 他的动态雕塑说明几个平衡的部件就能产生无穷的运动，是基于物理、营造氛围的 AR 物体的范本。
creators.based_zh: 罗克斯伯里，美国 / 萨谢，法国

creators.name: George Rickey
creators.role: Artist; kinetic sculptor of wind-driven blades
creators.bio: American sculptor (1907–2002) whose stainless-steel blades, lines and planes, balanced on precise bearings, swing and gyrate slowly in the slightest wind.
creators.why: He choreographed air with engineering alone, a lesson for AR objects that respond to wind, breath or device motion with calm, readable movement.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；风动不锈钢叶片的动态雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家（1907–2002），他的不锈钢叶片、线条和平面装在精密轴承上，在最轻的风中缓慢摆动、旋转。
creators.why_zh: 他只靠工程就编排了空气的舞蹈，启发 AR 物体以平静、易读的运动回应风、呼吸或手机的晃动。

creators.name: Len Lye
creators.role: Artist; kinetic sculptor and experimental filmmaker
creators.based: New York, US / New Plymouth, New Zealand
creators.bio: New Zealand-born artist (1901–1980) who painted directly on film and built 'tangible motion sculptures' of flexing steel that whip, sing and shimmer; many were realised full size after his death by the Len Lye Foundation.
creators.why: He treated motion as the material itself, which is how AR designers should think about animation in space.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；动态雕塑家与实验电影人
creators.bio_zh: 新西兰出生的艺术家（1901–1980），直接在胶片上作画，也制作会甩动、鸣响、闪烁的弹性钢“可触的运动雕塑”；许多作品在他去世后由 Len Lye 基金会按原尺寸实现。
creators.why_zh: 他把运动本身当作材料，这正是 AR 设计师看待空间动画的方式。
creators.based_zh: 纽约，美国 / 新普利茅斯，新西兰

creators.name: Takis
creators.role: Artist; sculptor of magnetism, light and sound
creators.bio: Greek artist Panayiotis Vassilakis (1925–2019) who made invisible forces visible: objects floating on magnetic fields, blinking 'Signaux' (signals) on tall rods, and musical sculptures played by magnets.
creators.why: He made invisible fields tangible, the same job AR does when it shows sensor data, forces or signals in space.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；以磁力、光和声音创作的雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 希腊艺术家帕纳约蒂斯·瓦西拉基斯（Takis，1925–2019），让看不见的力显形：悬浮在磁场中的物体、高杆上闪烁的“信号”（Signaux），以及由磁铁演奏的音乐雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他让看不见的场变得可感知，这正是 AR 在空间中显示传感器数据、力或信号时所做的事。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 雅典，希腊

creators.name: Pol Bury
creators.role: Artist; sculptor of slow kinetic movement
creators.bio: Belgian artist (1922–2005) who made movement almost imperceptible: balls and rods that creep on hidden motors, and polished steel fountains whose spheres tip and pour water in slow rhythms.
creators.why: He showed that slowness can be more captivating than speed, a useful lesson for calm, ambient AR animation.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；慢速动态雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 比利时艺术家（1922–2005），让运动几乎难以察觉：由隐藏电机缓慢推动的球和杆，以及抛光不锈钢球体慢慢倾斜、倒水的喷泉。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了慢比快更能吸引人，对平静、氛围型的 AR 动画很有启发。

creators.name: László Moholy-Nagy
creators.role: Artist; Bauhaus teacher and pioneer of light art
creators.bio: Hungarian artist (1895–1946) and Bauhaus teacher who built the Light Prop for an Electric Stage (1930), a motorised machine of metal and glass that throws moving shadows and reflections around a room, and filmed it as Ein Lichtspiel Schwarz Weiss Grau.
creators.why: He treated light and shadow as a spatial medium a century before AR, and imagined rooms that are made of projected light.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；包豪斯教师，光艺术先驱
creators.bio_zh: 匈牙利艺术家（1895–1946），包豪斯教师。他制作的《电动舞台光道具》（1930）是一台由金属和玻璃组成的电动机器，把移动的光影和反射投满整个房间，并拍成电影《光的游戏：黑白灰》。
creators.why_zh: 他在 AR 出现前一个世纪就把光与影当作空间媒介，设想由投射光构成的房间。
creators.based_zh: 柏林，德国 / 芝加哥，美国

creators.name: Gianni Colombo
creators.role: Artist; kinetic and programmed-art pioneer, member of Gruppo T
creators.bio: Italian artist (1937–1993) of Milan's Gruppo T who built pulsating reliefs and 'programmed environments' such as Spazio elastico (1967), a dark room of fluorescent elastic cords that slowly stretch and shift under UV light.
creators.why: His environments deform the space around the body instead of showing an image, a lesson in spatial, full-room AR effects.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；动态与程序艺术先驱，T 小组成员
creators.bio_zh: 意大利艺术家（1937–1993），米兰 T 小组（Gruppo T）成员，创作会脉动的浮雕和“程序化环境”，例如《弹性空间》（1967）：黑暗房间里荧光弹性绳在紫外光下缓慢拉伸、移位。
creators.why_zh: 他的环境不是展示图像，而是让身体周围的空间本身变形，这是全房间 AR 效果的一课。

creators.name: Eadweard Muybridge
creators.based: San Francisco and Philadelphia, US (born Kingston upon Thames, UK)
creators.bio: English-born photographer who used banks of tripwire-triggered cameras to split a galloping horse, athletes and animals into sequences of still frames, then projected them as moving images with his zoopraxiscope.
creators.why: He turned one invisible instant of motion into a row of frames you can walk along — the founding gesture of every motion trail and onion-skin in AR.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师；运动摄影先驱（1830–1904）
creators.bio_zh: 出生于英国的摄影师，用一排由绊线触发的相机把奔马、运动员和动物的动作拆成连续的静帧，再用自制的 zoopraxiscope 把它们投影成活动影像。
creators.why_zh: 他把看不见的一瞬运动切成一排可以沿着走过去看的画面——这是 AR 里所有运动残影和洋葱皮效果的起点。
creators.based_zh: 美国旧金山与费城（生于英国泰晤士河畔金斯顿）

creators.name: Étienne-Jules Marey
creators.bio: French physiologist who built the chronophotographic gun, fixed-plate chronophotography, bronze and plaster zoetrope sculptures of birds in flight, and smoke machines that made air currents visible.
creators.why: Marey drew motion as a single layered image and even as a physical sculpture — a direct model for turning tracked movement into 3D forms in AR.
creators.role_zh: 生理学家、连续摄影（chronophotography）的发明者（1830–1904）
creators.bio_zh: 法国生理学家，发明了连续摄影枪和单底片连续摄影，制作过鸟类飞行的石膏与青铜走马盘雕塑，还造出让气流显形的烟雾机。
creators.why_zh: Marey 把运动画成一张叠加的图像，甚至做成实体雕塑——这正是在 AR 中把追踪到的动作变成三维形体的直接范本。

creators.name: Harold "Doc" Edgerton
creators.role: Electrical engineer, MIT professor, father of stroboscopic photography (1903–1990)
creators.bio: MIT engineer who developed the electronic stroboscope and microsecond flash, freezing milk drops, bullets and athletes and layering multiple flashes into a single frame.
creators.why: Edgerton showed that a controlled flash of light can cut time into slices — the same trick behind strobe-based persistence effects in AR and 3D zoetropes.
creators.role_zh: 电气工程师、MIT 教授、频闪摄影之父（1903–1990）
creators.bio_zh: MIT 工程师，发明了电子频闪仪和微秒级闪光，定格了牛奶滴、子弹和运动员，也把多次闪光叠进同一张画面。
creators.why_zh: Edgerton 证明了一道受控的闪光就能把时间切成薄片——AR 中基于频闪的残影效果和 3D 走马盘用的正是同一招。

creators.name: Gjon Mili
creators.bio: Albanian-American photographer who worked with Harold Edgerton on stroboscopic and multiple-flash photography and, in 1949, photographed Pablo Picasso drawing in the air with a small light.
creators.why: His Picasso light drawings are the most famous proof that a gesture in empty air can become a lasting drawing — the core idea of every AR air-drawing tool.
creators.role_zh: LIFE 杂志摄影师与电影人（1904–1984）
creators.bio_zh: 阿尔巴尼亚裔美国摄影师，曾与 Harold Edgerton 一起研究频闪和多次闪光摄影；1949 年他拍下了 Pablo Picasso 用小手电在空中作画的照片。
creators.why_zh: 他拍的 Picasso 光绘最有力地证明了：在空中的一个手势也能变成留下来的画——这正是所有 AR 空中绘画工具的核心。
creators.based_zh: 美国纽约（生于阿尔巴尼亚科尔察）

creators.name: Frank & Lillian Gilbreth
creators.role: Industrial engineers; inventors of the cyclegraph and chronocyclegraph
creators.bio: American engineers and time-and-motion researchers who fixed small lights to workers' hands and photographed them with long exposures, producing light traces of movement and wire sculptures of the ideal motion path.
creators.why: Their cyclegraphs were the first light paintings made for analysis: motion turned into a 3D line you can study — exactly what AR hand tracking can now draw live.
creators.role_zh: 工业工程师；光迹摄影（cyclegraph）和计时光迹摄影（chronocyclegraph）的发明者
creators.bio_zh: 美国工程师和动作研究者，把小灯绑在工人手上用长曝光拍摄，得到动作的光迹，并据此弯出表示“理想动作路径”的铁丝雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他们的光迹照片是最早为分析而做的光绘：把动作变成一条可以研究的三维线——这正是今天 AR 手部追踪可以实时画出来的东西。
creators.based_zh: 美国新泽西州蒙特克莱尔

creators.name: Eric Staller
creators.bio: American artist known for 1970s 'Lightscapes' light-drawing photographs in New York streets and for public light works such as the Lightmobile, a Volkswagen Beetle covered in computer-controlled bulbs.
creators.why: He carried light drawing out of the studio into the street and onto moving objects — a reminder that AR content can ride on vehicles and people, not just stay on tables.
creators.role_zh: 光艺术家与设计师
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以 1970 年代在纽约街头拍摄的光绘作品《Lightscapes》，以及布满电脑控制灯泡的甲壳虫汽车《Lightmobile》等公共光艺术闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他把光绘从工作室带到街头、带到移动的物体上——提醒我们 AR 内容也可以跟着车和人走，而不只停在桌面上。
creators.based_zh: 荷兰阿姆斯特丹（生于美国纽约）

creators.name: Lichtfaktor
creators.bio: Cologne collective (Marcel Panne, Jan Leonardo Wöllert and friends) who since 2006 have made light-graffiti photographs and stop-motion films drawn frame by frame with flashlights, plus interactive light-painting setups for festivals.
creators.why: Lichtfaktor animates long-exposure drawings frame by frame, showing how hand-drawn light can live in real streets — the look many AR drawing apps try to reproduce live.
creators.role_zh: 光绘与光涂鸦团体
creators.bio_zh: 科隆的光绘团体（Marcel Panne、Jan Leonardo Wöllert 等），自 2006 年起用手电逐帧绘制光涂鸦照片和定格动画，也为艺术节做互动光绘装置。
creators.why_zh: Lichtfaktor 把长曝光光绘一帧一帧地做成动画，让手绘的光在真实街道里活起来——这正是许多 AR 绘画应用想实时做到的效果。

creators.name: Darren Pearson (DARIUSTWIN)
creators.bio: Los Angeles artist who draws glowing skeletons, dinosaurs and characters in the air with handheld lights and strings hundreds of long exposures into light-painting stop-motion films.
creators.why: His characters exist only as light traces placed in real landscapes — a hand-made version of AR characters anchored in the world.
creators.role_zh: 光绘艺术家与动画师
creators.bio_zh: 洛杉矶艺术家，用手持光源在空中画出发光的骷髅、恐龙和角色，再把几百张长曝光照片串成光绘定格动画。
creators.why_zh: 他的角色只以光迹的形式存在于真实风景中——就像手工做出来的、锚定在现实世界里的 AR 角色。

creators.name: Stephen Wilkes
creators.bio: American photographer whose 'Day to Night' series stitches up to 1,500 frames shot from one fixed position over 15 to 30 hours into a single image that flows from daylight to night.
creators.why: He shows time as a gradient across space in one picture — a strong model for AR views that let you scrub time by moving through a place.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师
creators.bio_zh: 美国摄影师，他的《Day to Night》系列在同一机位连续拍摄 15 到 30 小时、最多 1500 张照片，再合成一张从白天过渡到夜晚的画面。
creators.why_zh: 他在一张照片里把时间铺成空间上的渐变——这对“走动就能拖动时间轴”的 AR 视图是很好的范本。
creators.based_zh: 美国康涅狄格州韦斯特波特

creators.name: BERG (Jack Schulze, Matt Webb, Timo Arnall)
creators.bio: London design studio known for Little Printer, the 'Media Surfaces' films and experiments that made invisible technology visible, often with Timo Arnall's film work.
creators.why: BERG treated screens, networks and light as materials in physical space, a design stance that anticipated much of today's spatial computing.
creators.bio_zh: 伦敦设计工作室，以 Little Printer、《Media Surfaces》系列短片，以及让看不见的技术显形的实验闻名，许多影片由 Timo Arnall 拍摄。
creators.why_zh: BERG 把屏幕、网络和光都当作物理空间里的材料，这种设计立场预示了今天空间计算的许多方向。

creators.name: Timo Arnall
creators.bio: Designer and filmmaker who, with Jørn Knutsen and Einar Sneve Martinussen at the Oslo School of Architecture and Design, made the 'Immaterials' films that visualise RFID fields and WiFi signal strength with long-exposure light.
creators.why: Immaterials is the reference for making invisible data fields visible in real space — exactly what AR data overlays try to do.
creators.role_zh: 设计师与电影人；Immaterials 项目
creators.bio_zh: 设计师与电影人，与奥斯陆建筑与设计学院的 Jørn Knutsen、Einar Sneve Martinussen 合作拍摄了《Immaterials》系列，用长曝光的光把 RFID 场和 WiFi 信号强度画出来。
creators.why_zh: 《Immaterials》是“让看不见的数据场在真实空间里显形”的标杆——这正是 AR 数据叠加想做的事。
creators.based_zh: 挪威奥斯陆 / 英国伦敦

creators.name: Hiroshi Sugimoto (杉本博司)
creators.based: Tokyo, Japan and New York, US
creators.bio: Japanese artist whose 'Theaters' expose one photograph for the full length of a film, leaving a glowing white screen, and whose 'Seascapes' repeat one horizon of sea and sky across the world.
creators.why: His long exposures show that a camera can collapse hours into one frame — a way to think about AR that shows accumulated time instead of the present moment.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师、建筑师
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家。他的《Theaters》系列让一张底片曝光整部电影的时长，只留下发光的白色银幕；《Seascapes》系列在世界各地重复拍摄同一种海天之间的地平线。
creators.why_zh: 他的长曝光说明相机可以把几个小时压进一帧——让人思考 AR 不只显示此刻，也可以显示累积的时间。

creators.name: Norman McLaren
creators.role: Animator and filmmaker, National Film Board of Canada (1914–1987)
creators.bio: Scottish-Canadian animator at the NFB who painted directly on film, invented pixilation with live actors, and used optical printing to multiply dancers into trails of motion.
creators.why: McLaren treated time as a material you can print, stretch and repeat — the same levers AR designers use for echoes, trails and slow motion.
creators.role_zh: 加拿大国家电影局动画师与导演（1914–1987）
creators.bio_zh: 苏格兰裔加拿大动画师，在加拿大国家电影局（NFB）工作。他直接在胶片上作画，发明了用真人拍的“逐格真人动画”（pixilation），还用光学印片把舞者复制成一串运动轨迹。
creators.why_zh: McLaren 把时间当成可以印制、拉伸和重复的材料——AR 设计师做回声、拖尾和慢动作用的也是这些手段。
creators.based_zh: 加拿大蒙特利尔（生于苏格兰斯特灵）

creators.name: Adam Magyar
creators.bio: Hungarian artist who adapts industrial line-scan and high-speed cameras to record city crowds: 'Urban Flow' slit-scan panoramas of pedestrians and 'Stainless' ultra-slow films of commuters on passing subway platforms.
creators.why: His custom cameras show that changing how a sensor samples time produces a completely new picture of the same street — a lesson for AR camera effects.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师、影像艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 匈牙利艺术家，改装工业线扫描相机和高速摄影机来记录城市人群：《Urban Flow》用狭缝扫描拍下行人全景，《Stainless》用超慢速影像拍下列车驶过站台时的乘客。
creators.why_zh: 他的改装相机说明：只要改变传感器对时间的采样方式，同一条街就会变成全新的画面——这对 AR 相机特效很有启发。

creators.name: Zbigniew Rybczyński
creators.bio: Polish filmmaker and Academy Award winner whose 'Tango' layers 36 looping characters in one room, and who pioneered HD video compositing and slit-scan time effects in 'Steps' and 'The Fourth Dimension'.
creators.why: Tango is the clearest demonstration of many time loops sharing one space without colliding — a direct model for layering recorded people in AR.
creators.role_zh: 导演、录像艺术先驱
creators.bio_zh: 波兰导演、奥斯卡奖得主。《Tango》把 36 个循环动作的人物叠在同一个房间里；他还在《Steps》和《The Fourth Dimension》中开创了高清视频合成和狭缝扫描式的时间特效。
creators.why_zh: 《Tango》最清楚地展示了许多时间循环如何共享同一空间而互不碰撞——这是在 AR 里叠放录下来的人的直接范本。

creators.name: Michael Wesely
creators.bio: German photographer who builds pinhole-like cameras with extremely long exposures, recording construction sites such as Potsdamer Platz in Berlin and the Museum of Modern Art in New York over two to three years in a single image.
creators.why: His years-long exposures show a building rising as a ghostly overlay of its own history — the look of an AR 'time layer' over a site.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师
creators.bio_zh: 德国摄影师，自制超长曝光相机，在一张照片里记录柏林波茨坦广场、纽约现代艺术博物馆等工地两三年的变化。
creators.why_zh: 他长达数年的曝光让建筑在自身历史的幽灵般叠影中长出来——这就是 AR 叠加在场地上的“时间图层”应有的样子。

works.title: 329 prepared dc-motors, cotton balls, toluene tank
works.description: Inside a huge empty steel toluene tank, 329 small motors swing cotton balls on wires against the curved wall; the tapping multiplies into a roaring, echoing rain you stand inside.
works.description_zh: 在一个巨大的空钢制甲苯储罐里，329 个小电机甩动挂在铁丝上的棉球敲击弧形罐壁；敲击声层层叠加，变成一场包围你的轰鸣回声雨。
works.idea_en: The space is the instrument: an AR designer learns that simple agents placed along a real surface can make the architecture itself sound and feel alive.
works.idea_zh: 空间本身就是乐器：AR 设计者可以学到，沿真实表面布置的简单单元，能让建筑本身发声、显得有生命。
works.technique: Each dc-motor carries a short wire with a cotton ball that randomly strikes the tank wall; the large reverberant volume blends hundreds of slightly different rhythms into one texture.
works.technique_zh: 每个直流电机带着一段挂棉球的短铁丝，随机敲击罐壁；巨大的混响空间把数百个略有差异的节奏融为一种声音质感。
works.exercise_en: Scan a real wall with phone AR plane detection, scatter 100 virtual tappers along it that play a spatialised click with random timing, and walk through the resulting sound field. Twist: let the tapping rate follow how close the viewer stands.
works.exercise_zh: 用手机 AR 平面检测扫描一面真墙，沿墙随机布置 100 个虚拟“敲击器”，各自以随机节奏播放空间化的咔哒声，然后走进这片声场。变体：让敲击频率随观众离墙的距离变化。

works.title: 658 prepared dc-motors, cotton balls, cardboard boxes 70x70x70cm
works.description: A wall of stacked cardboard boxes, each with motors inside swinging cotton balls, fills a hall with a soft, crackling drizzle that changes as you walk along it.
works.description_zh: 一整面由纸箱堆成的墙，每个箱子里都有电机甩动棉球；柔和噼啪的“细雨声”充满展厅，沿墙走动时声音随之变化。
works.idea_en: A grid of identical cells becomes a landscape of sound when each cell is slightly out of sync; in AR, repetition plus tiny randomness reads as life.
works.idea_zh: 当每个格子稍微不同步时，一格格相同的单元就成了一片声音风景；在 AR 里，重复加上一点随机就显得有生命。
works.technique: Motors inside each box strike the cardboard from within, turning every box into a resonator; stacking them into a wall creates a spatial array of sound sources.
works.technique_zh: 每个箱子里的电机从内部敲击纸板，把每个箱子变成共鸣箱；把它们堆成墙，就形成一个空间化的声源阵列。
works.exercise_en: Stack a 10×10 grid of virtual boxes against a real wall in WebXR, give each one a looping rattle sound with random phase, and record a walk past it with spatial audio. Twist: let each box you look at fall silent.
works.exercise_zh: 在 WebXR 中沿真墙堆出 10×10 的虚拟纸箱，每个箱子播放相位随机的循环嘎嗒声，带着空间音频走过并录下来。变体：被你注视的箱子会安静下来。

works.title: 275 prepared dc-motors, filler wire 1.0mm
works.description: Hundreds of thin wires sprout from motors mounted across a room's walls and spin, whirring and scratching, so the whole space shivers like a field of insects.
works.description_zh: 数百根细铁丝从装在墙上的电机中伸出并旋转，发出嗡嗡的刮擦声，整个空间像一片昆虫的原野般颤动。
works.idea_en: Covering an architectural surface with one repeated gesture reframes the whole room; AR can do the same by instancing one tiny behaviour across a scanned mesh.
works.idea_zh: 用同一个动作覆盖整片建筑表面，就能重塑整个房间；AR 可以把一个微小行为批量实例化到扫描出的网格上来做到这一点。
works.technique: Each motor spins a short length of 1 mm welding filler wire that scrapes the wall; the material list is the entire system (year from the exhibition, likely 2011).
works.technique_zh: 每个电机旋转一小段 1 毫米焊丝，刮擦墙面；材料清单就是整个系统（年份依展览推测，约 2011 年）。
works.exercise_en: Use LiDAR scene reconstruction to get the room mesh, instance 500 short spinning wires normal to the surfaces, and add a faint scratch sound to each. Twist: let wires near the viewer's hand spin faster.
works.exercise_zh: 用 LiDAR 场景重建获得房间网格，沿表面法线实例化 500 根旋转的短铁丝，每根加一点刮擦声。变体：靠近观众手部的铁丝转得更快。

works.title: 192 prepared dc-motors, wooden sticks 2.4m
works.description: Long wooden sticks hang from motors in a dense grid and knock against each other and the floor, creating a forest of clattering, swaying lines you can walk around.
works.description_zh: 长长的木棍挂在网格状排列的电机上，彼此碰撞、敲击地面，形成一片可以绕行的、摇摆作响的线之森林。
works.idea_en: A forest of long lines makes a room's height and depth legible; AR designers can use vertical elements the same way to reveal space.
works.idea_zh: 一片长线之林让房间的高度和纵深一目了然；AR 设计者也可以用竖向元素来揭示空间。
works.technique: Motors at the top of each 2.4 m stick create a small eccentric wobble that propagates down the stick, so the tips tap the floor in unpredictable patterns.
works.technique_zh: 每根 2.4 米木棍顶端的电机产生小幅偏心摆动，沿木棍向下传递，使棍尖以难以预测的方式敲击地面。
works.exercise_en: Hang 200 virtual sticks from the ceiling of a scanned room in AR Foundation, drive each with a small random pendulum motion and a knock sound on floor contact. Twist: let the sticks part like curtains as the viewer walks through.
works.exercise_zh: 在 AR Foundation 中从扫描房间的天花板垂下 200 根虚拟木棍，用小幅随机摆动驱动，并在触地时发出敲击声。变体：观众走过时，木棍像帘子一样分开。

works.title: Untitled Sound Objects (with Pe Lang)
works.description: A series of small wall objects by Pe Lang and Zimoun in which motors make strings, paper and wires rustle and buzz, each box its own tiny mechanical sound machine.
works.description_zh: Pe Lang 与 Zimoun 合作的一系列小型壁挂装置，电机让线、纸和铁丝沙沙作响、嗡嗡振动，每个盒子都是一台小小的机械声音机器。
works.idea_en: Small, framed sound objects show that an AR piece can be intimate and wall-sized rather than room-sized.
works.idea_zh: 小巧的框装声音物件说明，AR 作品也可以是贴在墙上的亲密小件，而不必占满整个房间。
works.technique: Each object pairs a simple motor with one material so that the sound and the motion are the same event, visible and audible at once.
works.technique_zh: 每件作品把一个简单电机和一种材料配在一起，让声音和运动成为同一个事件，同时看得见、听得见。
works.exercise_en: Build three framed virtual boxes on a real wall with image tracking, each animating one material (string, paper, wire) with a matching sound. Twist: let visitors tap a box to change its material.
works.exercise_zh: 用图像追踪在真墙上放三个带框的虚拟盒子，各自让一种材料（线、纸、铁丝）动起来并配上相应的声音。变体：观众点击盒子即可更换材料。

works.title: Square Wave
works.description: A square grid of suspended wooden blocks rises and falls as two perpendicular waves pass through it, forming a rippling surface that constantly crosses and recombines.
works.description_zh: 一个由悬挂木块组成的方形网格随着两道相互垂直的波起伏，形成不断交错又重组的涟漪曲面。
works.idea_en: Two simple sine waves added together already produce a surface that feels alive; AR motion can be built from the same small set of summed waves.
works.idea_zh: 两条简单正弦波相加，就能产生一个感觉有生命的曲面；AR 中的运动也可以用同样少量叠加的波构建。
works.technique: Two rows of camshafts each generate a wave; strings running over pulleys sum the two displacements at every grid point, so each block's height is x-wave plus y-wave.
works.technique_zh: 两排凸轮轴各自产生一道波，绕过滑轮的绳子在每个网格点把两个位移相加，因此每个木块的高度等于 x 向波加 y 向波。
works.exercise_en: Place a 20×20 grid of floating cubes over a real table in phone AR and set each height to sin(x+t)+sin(y+t). Twist: let the viewer's phone position set the phase of one of the waves.
works.exercise_zh: 用手机 AR 在真桌上方放一个 20×20 的悬浮方块阵列，每块高度设为 sin(x+t)+sin(y+t)。变体：用观众手机的位置决定其中一道波的相位。

works.title: Magic Wave
works.description: Hundreds of hanging points driven by a stack of turning wheels trace an undulating sheet that looks like ocean swell frozen in wood and string; the video shows how it is built.
works.description_zh: 数百个悬挂点由一叠转动的轮子驱动，勾勒出一张起伏的面，像被木头和绳子定格的海浪；视频展示了它的搭建过程。
works.idea_en: Seeing the mechanism beside the effect teaches AR designers to expose the 'engine' of an effect as part of the experience.
works.idea_zh: 把机械结构和效果并置展示，提醒 AR 设计者可以把效果背后的“引擎”也作为体验的一部分展示出来。
works.technique: Rotating eccentric wheels act as wave generators and a network of strings mechanically adds their motions at each hanging point (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 偏心轮的转动充当波的发生器，绳网在每个悬挂点上机械地叠加它们的运动（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Build a WebXR scene where three virtual wheels hover beside a hanging mesh and visibly drive it through connecting lines. Twist: let viewers grab a wheel and change its speed.
works.exercise_zh: 在 WebXR 中做三个悬浮的虚拟轮子，通过可见的连线驱动旁边一张悬挂的网面。变体：让观众抓住轮子改变转速。

works.title: Nebula
works.description: A vast cloud of hanging glass pieces fills an atrium and slowly swells and folds in waves, catching light like a nebula breathing above the lobby.
works.description_zh: 一大片悬挂的玻璃块充满中庭，以波浪缓缓鼓起、折叠，捕捉光线，仿佛一团星云在大堂上方呼吸。
works.idea_en: A volume of points moving together reads as one creature; AR particle clouds gain presence when they move as coherent waves rather than noise.
works.idea_zh: 一整块点阵一起运动时会被读作一个生命体；AR 粒子云如果以连贯的波而非噪声运动，会更有存在感。
works.technique: Motor-driven camshafts above the ceiling feed summed wave motions down thousands of cables to the glass elements, turning a lobby into a 3D wave field.
works.technique_zh: 天花板上方由电机驱动的凸轮轴，通过数千根缆绳把叠加的波动传给玻璃元件，把大堂变成一个三维波场。
works.exercise_en: Fill a real room with 2,000 virtual glass shards in phone AR and move them with two summed 3D waves; add a refractive shader. Twist: let the cloud slowly lean toward the brightest window.
works.exercise_zh: 用手机 AR 在真实房间里放 2000 片虚拟玻璃，用两道叠加的三维波驱动，并加上折射着色器。变体：让这团“星云”慢慢倾向最亮的窗户。

works.title: Caterpillar with Green Stripe
works.description: A segmented wooden caterpillar undulates along its length as a crank turns, capturing the wave that runs down a real caterpillar's body.
works.description_zh: 一只分节的木制毛毛虫随着曲柄转动沿身体起伏，捕捉到了真实毛毛虫身上流动的波。
works.idea_en: A creature's liveliness can come from a single traveling wave; AR characters can feel alive with nothing more than a phase-shifted loop.
works.idea_zh: 一个生物的灵动可以只来自一道行波；AR 角色只要一个带相位差的循环就能显得有生命。
works.technique: A cam per segment, each offset by a fixed angle on a shared shaft, lifts the segments in sequence so the wave travels along the body.
works.technique_zh: 每节对应一个凸轮，它们在同一根轴上依次错开固定角度，按顺序抬起各节，使波沿身体传递。
works.exercise_en: Build a 12-segment creature crawling across a real floor in Lens Studio, lifting each segment with sin(t - k*i). Twist: make the wave reverse when the camera comes close.
works.exercise_zh: 在 Lens Studio 中做一只 12 节的生物在真实地面爬行，每节以 sin(t - k*i) 抬起。变体：镜头靠近时，波反向传递。

works.title: Wind Veil
works.description: Tens of thousands of small hinged aluminium panels cover a parking-garage façade and flutter in the wind, so gusts sweep across the building as visible ripples of light.
works.description_zh: 数万块铰接的小铝片覆盖停车楼立面，随风翻动，阵风掠过时在建筑上形成可见的光之涟漪。
works.idea_en: Making an invisible force visible across a surface is AR's core promise; Kahn does it at building scale with no electronics.
works.idea_zh: 让看不见的力在表面上显形，正是 AR 的核心承诺；Kahn 在建筑尺度上做到了，而且不用任何电子元件。
works.technique: Each panel hangs freely on a hinge; wind pressure tilts it and changes how it reflects sky and sun, so the façade becomes a real-time map of airflow (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 每片铝片自由挂在铰链上，风压使它倾斜并改变对天空与阳光的反射，整面立面成为实时的气流地图（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Cover a real building façade in WebXR with a grid of small reflective flaps that tilt with live wind data from a weather API. Twist: let the viewer blow into the microphone to add a gust.
works.exercise_zh: 在 WebXR 中给一栋真实建筑立面铺满小反光片，用天气 API 的实时风速数据让它们翻动。变体：观众对着麦克风吹气可以加一阵风。

works.title: Articulated Cloud
works.description: The façade of the Children's Museum of Pittsburgh is a veil of thousands of translucent squares that shimmer in the wind like a cloud wrapped around the building.
works.description_zh: 匹兹堡儿童博物馆的立面是一层由数千块半透明方片组成的帘幕，随风闪动，像一朵裹住建筑的云。
works.idea_en: A soft, moving skin makes architecture feel weather-sensitive; AR façades can borrow this idea of a responsive veil over a fixed structure.
works.idea_zh: 柔软而流动的外皮让建筑显得对天气敏感；AR 立面可以借用这种“覆盖在固定结构上的会回应的帘幕”。
works.technique: Lightweight plastic tiles on hinged mounts respond individually to wind and scatter daylight, creating a large-scale analog display of turbulence.
works.technique_zh: 轻质塑料片装在铰接支架上，各自对风作出反应并散射日光，形成一个大尺度的湍流模拟显示屏。
works.exercise_en: Anchor a translucent tile veil to a real building with geospatial AR and animate each tile with Perlin-noise wind. Twist: make the veil part where people walk underneath.
works.exercise_zh: 用地理空间 AR 在真实建筑上锚定一层半透明方片帘幕，用 Perlin 噪声风驱动每一片。变体：有人从下面走过时，帘幕分开。

works.title: Tornado
works.description: A column of fog twists into a tall, stable vortex inside a frame; visitors can put their hands into it and watch the tornado bend and reform.
works.description_zh: 一根雾柱在框架内扭成高而稳定的漩涡；观众可以把手伸进去，看着龙卷风弯折又复原。
works.idea_en: Fog is a way to see flow; AR can use particles in the same way to show otherwise invisible currents, and invite the hand to disturb them.
works.idea_zh: 雾是看见流动的方法；AR 也可以用粒子展示原本看不见的气流，并邀请人用手去扰动它。
works.technique: Fans on top pull air upward while angled vents add rotation, and a fog machine seeds the flow so the vortex becomes visible (year approximate; Kahn has built tornados since the 1980s).
works.technique_zh: 顶部风扇向上抽气，倾斜的风口带来旋转，雾机向气流中注入雾气使漩涡显形（年份为估计；Kahn 自 1980 年代起就在制作龙卷风装置）。
works.exercise_en: Spawn a particle vortex on a real table in phone AR and let hand tracking push the particles away. Twist: let the vortex slowly drift toward the loudest sound in the room.
works.exercise_zh: 用手机 AR 在真桌上生成一个粒子漩涡，并用手部追踪把粒子推开。变体：让漩涡慢慢漂向房间里最响的声音。

works.title: Technorama Facade
works.description: The façade of the Swiss Science Center Technorama in Winterthur is covered with tens of thousands of small hinged aluminium plates that ripple in the wind, turning the building into a wind display.
works.description_zh: 瑞士温特图尔 Technorama 科学中心的立面覆盖着数万块铰接小铝板，随风起伏，整座建筑变成了风的显示屏。
works.idea_en: Every pixel here is a physical sensor and actuator in one, a reminder that the best AR displays may be the world's own surfaces reacting.
works.idea_zh: 这里的每个“像素”既是传感器又是执行器，提醒我们最好的 AR 显示也许就是世界自身表面的反应。
works.technique: Free-swinging aluminium plates mounted in a grid reflect the sky at varying angles, so pressure waves in the wind appear as moving patterns of light and shadow.
works.technique_zh: 网格排列的铝板自由摆动，以不同角度反射天空，风中的压力波于是呈现为流动的光影图案。
works.exercise_en: Map a grid of virtual plates onto a façade photo with image tracking and drive them with a fluid simulation. Twist: let the plates spell a word only when the wind stops.
works.exercise_zh: 用图像追踪把虚拟金属片阵列贴到立面照片上，用流体模拟驱动。变体：只有风停时，金属片才拼出一个词。

works.title: Wind Arbor
works.description: A tall glass façade at Marina Bay Sands in Singapore is lined with hundreds of thousands of small hinged metal flaps that flutter with the wind and cast moving shadows into the atrium.
works.description_zh: 新加坡滨海湾金沙一面高大的玻璃立面上挂满数十万片铰接的小金属片，随风颤动，把流动的光影投进中庭。
works.idea_en: Shadows cast inside tell visitors what is happening outside; AR can likewise let outdoor data leak indoors as light and shadow.
works.idea_zh: 投进室内的影子告诉人们外面正在发生什么；AR 同样可以让户外数据以光影的形式渗进室内。
works.technique: Wind moves each flap independently and the changing pattern filters sunlight entering the building, creating a kinetic sunscreen (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 风让每片金属片独立摆动，变化的图案过滤进入建筑的阳光，形成一面动态遮阳幕（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Project virtual flapping shadows onto a real floor in AR, driven by live wind speed from a weather API. Twist: tie the shadow density to the day's air quality.
works.exercise_zh: 在 AR 中把虚拟的翻动影子投到真实地面上，由天气 API 的实时风速驱动。变体：让影子的密度对应当天的空气质量。

works.title: Di-Octo
works.description: Two stacked stainless-steel spheres of spoon-like cups turn in opposite directions in the wind, producing a mesmerising interference pattern that seems to fold in on itself.
works.description_zh: 两个上下叠放、由勺状杯片组成的不锈钢球体在风中反向旋转，产生一种仿佛向内折叠的迷幻干涉图案。
works.idea_en: Counter-rotating layers create depth and moiré; AR designers can use layered opposite motions to make a virtual object feel volumetric and alive.
works.idea_zh: 反向旋转的层次产生纵深与摩尔纹；AR 设计者可以用相反运动的叠层，让虚拟物体显得立体而有生命。
works.technique: Precision-machined cups catch wind on nested rotating frames; because each frame spins at its own rate, the sculpture never repeats the same configuration.
works.technique_zh: 精密加工的杯片在嵌套的旋转框架上兜风，每个框架以各自的速度转动，雕塑永远不会重复同一姿态。
works.exercise_en: Build two nested rings of reflective cups in phone AR spinning in opposite directions at speeds driven by the phone's microphone wind noise. Twist: let the viewer's walking speed set the rotation.
works.exercise_zh: 在手机 AR 中做两层嵌套的反光杯片环，以相反方向旋转，转速由麦克风收到的风噪决定。变体：用观众的步行速度决定转速。

works.title: In Cloud Light III
works.description: A tall wind sculpture of stacked, spoke-mounted stainless discs rotates in the breeze, each tier turning at its own pace so the form constantly shimmers and reconfigures.
works.description_zh: 一件高大的风动雕塑，由层层叠放、装在辐条上的不锈钢圆片组成，每一层以自己的节奏转动，整体不断闪烁、重组。
works.idea_en: Reflection plus rotation make a sculpture borrow colour from the sky; AR materials that reflect the real environment gain the same site-specific shimmer.
works.idea_zh: 反射加旋转，让雕塑从天空借来颜色；能反射真实环境的 AR 材质也能获得同样因地而异的闪光。
works.technique: Each tier is balanced on its own bearing and sized so that the same wind drives it at a different speed, producing phasing patterns (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 每一层都装在独立轴承上并经过配重，大小各异，同一阵风驱动它们以不同速度转动，产生相位交错的图案（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Place a stack of five reflective rings in a real park with geospatial AR, use environment probes for real reflections, and spin each at a slightly different rate. Twist: link the spin to the live local wind speed.
works.exercise_zh: 用地理空间 AR 在真实公园里放一座五层反光圆环塔，用环境探针获得真实反射，每层转速略有不同。变体：把转速和当地实时风速绑定。

works.title: Rio 2016 Olympic Cauldron
works.description: For the Rio 2016 Olympic opening ceremony, a small cauldron flame was framed by a huge kinetic sun of reflective spheres and plates that spun and pulsed around it.
works.description_zh: 在 2016 年里约奥运会开幕式上，一个小小的圣火被一轮巨大的动态“太阳”环绕，反光球体和金属板围着它旋转、脉动。
works.idea_en: A small real flame amplified by a moving reflective frame shows how AR can enlarge a modest real event rather than replace it.
works.idea_zh: 一团小小的真实火焰，被一个运动的反光框架放大：AR 可以放大一个朴素的真实事件，而不是取代它。
works.technique: A motorised rotating structure of polished stainless elements reflects and multiplies the flame's light, turning a small fire into a stadium-scale sun.
works.technique_zh: 由抛光不锈钢元件组成的电动旋转结构反射并倍增火焰的光，把小火苗变成体育场尺度的太阳。
works.exercise_en: Detect a candle or phone flashlight with the camera, then surround it in AR with a rotating ring of mirrors that reflect its glow. Twist: let the ring grow as more people gather around.
works.exercise_zh: 用摄像头识别一支蜡烛或手机手电筒，在 AR 中用一圈旋转的镜面环绕它、反射它的光。变体：围观的人越多，光环越大。

works.title: Machine with Concrete
works.description: A motor spins the first gear fast; through a chain of twelve 1:50 gear reductions the last gear is embedded in a block of concrete, since it would take over two trillion years to turn once.
works.description_zh: 电机让第一个齿轮飞快转动；经过十二级 1:50 的减速，最后一个齿轮被浇进一块混凝土里，因为它转一圈需要超过两万亿年。
works.idea_en: Motion can be made to disappear into deep time; an AR piece can show a process whose end lies far beyond a human life.
works.idea_zh: 运动可以消失在深远的时间里；AR 作品可以展示一个终点远超人类寿命的过程。
works.technique: Twelve worm-style reductions of 50:1 each multiply to 50^12, so the output speed is effectively zero and the concrete never feels it.
works.technique_zh: 十二级 50:1 减速相乘得到 50 的 12 次方，输出转速几乎为零，混凝土永远感觉不到它。
works.exercise_en: Anchor a virtual gear train to a real wall in AR that ends inside a real object, with each gear's real speed computed and displayed. Twist: display how many years until the last gear completes one turn, counting down live.
works.exercise_zh: 在 AR 中把一串虚拟齿轮锚定在真墙上，最后一个齿轮“卡进”一个真实物体，按真实比例计算并显示每个齿轮的转速。变体：实时倒计时最后一个齿轮转完一圈还需要多少年。

works.title: Machine with Wishbone
works.description: A tiny wire machine drags a chicken wishbone along a circular track, so the bone seems to walk forward with a strange, earnest gait.
works.description_zh: 一台铁丝做的小机器拖着一根鸡的许愿骨沿圆形轨道前进，让骨头看起来正用一种奇怪而认真的步态走路。
works.idea_en: Giving a found object a gait gives it a character; AR can animate everyday objects with minimal, well-chosen motion.
works.idea_zh: 给一件拾得物一种步态，就给了它性格；AR 可以用最少、最恰当的动作让日常物件活起来。
works.technique: A crank mechanism pushes and lifts the wishbone in a stepping cycle, and the whole machine rotates slowly so the walk becomes an endless loop.
works.technique_zh: 曲柄机构以步行周期推动并抬起许愿骨，整台机器缓慢转动，让这段行走变成无尽的循环。
works.exercise_en: Scan an everyday object (fork, clothes peg) with photogrammetry and give it a two-step walk cycle across a real table in AR. Twist: let it stop and turn toward whoever speaks.
works.exercise_zh: 用摄影测量扫描一件日常物件（叉子、衣夹），在 AR 中给它一个两步行走循环，让它在真桌上走。变体：谁说话，它就停下转向谁。

works.title: Margot's Cat
works.description: A tiny chair is repeatedly flung upward and caught by a delicate wire mechanism, so it seems to leap and land again like a playful cat.
works.description_zh: 一把小椅子被纤细的铁丝机构一次次抛起又接住，像一只贪玩的猫一样跳起、落下。
works.idea_en: Timing and anticipation make inanimate objects feel intentional; AR animations should borrow the rhythm of a real creature rather than smooth tweens (year approximate).
works.idea_zh: 时机与预备动作让无生命的物件显得有意图；AR 动画应借用真实生物的节奏，而不是平滑的补间（年份为估计）。
works.technique: A cam-driven arm stores and releases energy, launching the chair in a ballistic arc before a second arm catches it, repeated as a loop.
works.technique_zh: 由凸轮驱动的摆臂蓄能后释放，把椅子沿抛物线弹出，再由另一只摆臂接住，如此循环。
works.exercise_en: Make a small virtual chair on a real desk jump along a physics arc every few seconds in phone AR, with squash-and-stretch on landing. Twist: let it jump only when the viewer looks away.
works.exercise_zh: 在手机 AR 中让真桌上的一把虚拟小椅子每隔几秒沿物理抛物线跳一次，落地时加挤压拉伸。变体：只有观众移开视线时它才跳。

works.title: Cory's Yellow Chair
works.description: A small yellow chair continuously bursts apart into its separate pieces, which float outward and then come back together into a whole chair again.
works.description_zh: 一把黄色小椅子不断地炸开成零件，零件向外飘散，再重新合拢成一把完整的椅子。
works.idea_en: The exploded view is a powerful AR move: taking a real object apart in space and reassembling it explains it and delights at once.
works.idea_zh: 爆炸视图是 AR 中很有力的一招：把真实物体在空间中拆开再拼回去，既能讲解，又令人愉悦。
works.technique: Each chair part is held on its own wire arm driven by a shared cam system, so all pieces move out and back in coordinated radial paths.
works.technique_zh: 椅子的每个部件由各自的铁丝臂支撑，由同一套凸轮系统驱动，所有部件沿协调的径向路径散开又收回。
works.exercise_en: Scan a real chair, split the model into parts in Reality Composer or Unity, and animate an exploded view that loops around the real chair in AR. Twist: let the viewer's distance control how far the parts fly apart.
works.exercise_zh: 扫描一把真椅子，在 Reality Composer 或 Unity 中拆成零件，在 AR 中围绕真椅子循环播放爆炸视图。变体：观众离得越近，零件飞得越远。

works.title: AD INFINITUM
works.description: A tall outdoor wind sculpture whose looping stainless-steel forms rotate in the breeze, drawing an endless figure that shifts as you walk around it.
works.description_zh: 一座高大的户外风动雕塑，环形的不锈钢形体在微风中旋转，勾勒出一个随你绕行而变化的无尽图形。
works.idea_en: A form that reads differently from every angle rewards walking around it, the key behaviour to design for in world-anchored AR.
works.idea_zh: 从每个角度看都不一样的形体会奖励绕行，这是世界锚定 AR 最需要设计的行为。
works.technique: Balanced stainless-steel elements on low-friction bearings turn in light wind, and their curved loops overlap into changing silhouettes (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 配重平衡的不锈钢构件装在低摩擦轴承上，微风即可转动，弯曲的环相互重叠形成不断变化的轮廓（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Place a looping virtual sculpture in an open square with geospatial AR, rotating slowly on two axes. Twist: reveal a hidden symbol that only aligns from one walking position.
works.exercise_zh: 用地理空间 AR 在开阔广场上放一座环形虚拟雕塑，绕两根轴缓慢旋转。变体：藏一个只有走到特定位置才会对齐的符号。

works.title: UNION 3
works.description: A wind-driven kinetic sculpture in Qingdao, China, that combines turning stainless-steel forms with coloured light, so it changes from a daytime sculpture into a night-time light work.
works.description_zh: 位于中国青岛的一座风动雕塑，旋转的不锈钢形体与彩色灯光结合，白天是雕塑，夜晚变成光的作品。
works.idea_en: Designing for both day and night states is essential in outdoor AR, where lighting conditions change what content reads well.
works.idea_zh: 为白天和夜晚分别设计状态，在户外 AR 中至关重要，因为光照条件会改变内容的可读性。
works.technique: Wind turns the steel elements while integrated LEDs colour them after dark, adding a second, programmable layer to the physical motion (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 风转动钢构件，内置 LED 在天黑后为其着色，为物理运动叠加一层可编程的第二层次（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Build an AR sculpture that switches between a reflective day material and a glowing night material using the device's ambient light estimate. Twist: let the colour follow the city's live temperature.
works.exercise_zh: 做一个 AR 雕塑，根据设备的环境光估计在白天反光材质和夜晚发光材质之间切换。变体：让颜色跟随城市的实时气温。

works.title: SENSE #1
works.description: An interactive light mural and sculpture that doubles as a clock, lighting up in response to people passing and to the time of day.
works.description_zh: 一件互动的光壁画兼雕塑，同时也是一座时钟，会随路人经过和一天中的时间而亮起。
works.idea_en: Combining ambient information (time) with response to presence makes a public piece useful and playful at once, a good pattern for civic AR.
works.idea_zh: 把环境信息（时间）与对人的回应结合，让公共作品既有用又好玩，是城市 AR 的好模式。
works.technique: Presence sensors trigger light sequences while a clock logic shifts the base pattern through the day (details not documented; likely motion sensors).
works.technique_zh: 存在感应器触发灯光序列，时钟逻辑则让基础图案随时间推移变化（细节未公开，可能是运动传感器）。
works.exercise_en: Anchor an AR clock to a real wall whose hands are made of light particles that scatter when someone walks by. Twist: let the particles reassemble a little slower each hour.
works.exercise_zh: 在真墙上锚定一个 AR 时钟，指针由光粒子组成，有人走过时粒子散开。变体：每过一小时，粒子重新聚合得更慢一点。

works.title: Asinas
works.description: Two interlocking spirals of white segments rotate at slightly different speeds, so a wave appears to travel through the sculpture while nothing actually moves forward.
works.description_zh: 两组相互嵌套的白色螺旋片以略有不同的速度旋转，仿佛有一道波穿过雕塑，其实没有任何东西真正向前移动。
works.idea_en: Apparent motion can emerge from two rotations; AR designers can create flowing effects without moving objects, just by phasing their parts.
works.idea_zh: 表观运动可以从两个旋转中浮现；AR 设计者不必移动物体，只需让部件错相就能制造流动感。
works.technique: A single motor drives two concentric spiral assemblies through gears with a slightly different ratio, so their relative phase drifts and creates travelling interference.
works.technique_zh: 一个电机通过传动比略有差异的齿轮驱动两组同心螺旋，它们的相对相位不断漂移，形成行进的干涉纹。
works.exercise_en: Build two nested virtual helices in phone AR rotating at speeds 1.00 and 1.03 and watch the moiré wave appear. Twist: let the viewer's tilt change the ratio.
works.exercise_zh: 在手机 AR 中做两条嵌套的虚拟螺旋，转速分别为 1.00 和 1.03，观察摩尔纹波浪出现。变体：让手机的倾角改变转速比。

works.title: Cubes
works.description: A column of cubes turns slowly, each at a slightly different speed, so the stack twists into ever-changing spirals and then realigns into a straight tower.
works.description_zh: 一列方块缓慢转动，每块的速度略有不同，于是整叠方块扭成不断变化的螺旋，然后又重新对齐成一座笔直的塔。
works.idea_en: Slow phase drift between identical parts creates a narrative arc of order, chaos and order again, a simple structure for time-based AR pieces.
works.idea_zh: 相同部件之间缓慢的相位漂移构成“有序—混乱—再有序”的叙事弧，是时间性 AR 作品的一种简单结构。
works.technique: A gear train gives each cube a marginally different rotation rate, so the stack only returns to alignment after a long common period (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 齿轮组给每个方块稍微不同的转速，只有经过很长的公共周期后整叠方块才会重新对齐（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Stack 20 virtual cubes on a real shelf in AR, rotating each at 1 + i/100 speed, and time how long until they realign. Twist: make the tower chime when it becomes straight again.
works.exercise_zh: 在 AR 中于真实书架上叠 20 个虚拟方块，第 i 块以 1 + i/100 的速度旋转，计时它们多久重新对齐。变体：塔重新对齐时发出一声钟鸣。

works.title: Phaser
works.description: A drawing machine whose linked rotating arms guide a pen to trace dense, evolving geometric patterns on paper, recording the machine's motion as a drawing.
works.description_zh: 一台绘图机器，联动的旋转臂引导笔在纸上描出密集而不断演化的几何图案，把机器的运动记录成一幅画。
works.idea_en: The drawing is a record of motion over time; AR can leave persistent trails that turn movement into a lasting artefact.
works.idea_zh: 画作是运动随时间留下的记录；AR 可以留下持续的轨迹，把运动变成可保存的作品。
works.technique: Two or more rotating arms with slightly different periods combine like a harmonograph, so the pen path slowly precesses into a complex figure (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 两根或多根周期略有不同的旋转臂像谐振记录仪一样组合，笔的路径缓慢进动，形成复杂图形（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Attach a virtual pen to two rotating virtual arms on a real table in phone AR and let it draw a persistent line. Twist: let viewers nudge one arm's speed with a slider and compare drawings.
works.exercise_zh: 在手机 AR 中给真桌上的两根虚拟旋转臂装一支虚拟笔，让它画出持久的线。变体：让观众用滑块微调其中一根臂的速度，并比较不同的画。

works.title: Sisyphus
works.description: A steel ball rolls silently through a bed of sand, pulled by a hidden magnet, drawing spirals and flower patterns that it then erases with the next drawing.
works.description_zh: 一颗钢珠在隐藏磁铁的牵引下无声地滚过沙床，画出螺旋和花形图案，又在画下一幅时将其抹去。
works.idea_en: A single moving point leaves a readable trace in a real material; AR trails that interact with real surfaces can feel as calm and physical as this.
works.idea_zh: 一个移动的点在真实材料中留下可读的痕迹；与真实表面互动的 AR 轨迹也可以像这样安静而有质感。
works.technique: A two-axis polar robot under the table moves a magnet along programmed paths; the ball follows above and displaces sand, so the path becomes a drawing.
works.technique_zh: 桌下的两轴极坐标机器人沿预设路径移动磁铁，上面的钢珠随之移动并推开沙子，路径就成了画。
works.exercise_en: Detect a real tabletop in phone AR and roll a virtual ball that carves a persistent groove into a sand shader along a parametric path. Twist: let the viewer draw the path with a finger and watch the ball follow it.
works.exercise_zh: 用手机 AR 识别真实桌面，让一颗虚拟钢珠沿参数化路径在沙质着色器上刻出持续的沟纹。变体：观众用手指画路径，钢珠随后跟着走。

works.title: Blooms
works.description: 3D-printed sculptures spin under a strobe light and appear to bloom endlessly, petals flowing outward from the centre like a living flower.
works.description_zh: 3D 打印的雕塑在频闪灯下旋转，仿佛在无限绽放，花瓣从中心不断向外涌出，像一朵活着的花。
works.idea_en: When the flash is synchronised to the geometry, a static object becomes animation; AR depends on the same sync between rendering and real motion.
works.idea_zh: 当闪光与几何结构同步时，静态物体就成了动画；AR 同样依赖渲染与真实运动的同步。
works.technique: Petals are placed at successive golden-angle (137.5°) steps; spinning so that one rotation of 137.5° happens between flashes makes each petal appear to move to its neighbour's position.
works.technique_zh: 花瓣按黄金角（137.5°）依次排列；让雕塑在两次闪光之间正好转过 137.5°，每片花瓣看起来就移到了相邻花瓣的位置。
works.exercise_en: Generate a golden-angle bloom mesh in three.js WebXR and rotate it by exactly 137.5° per frame on a real table. Twist: let the viewer change the angle slightly and watch the bloom spiral in reverse.
works.exercise_zh: 在 three.js WebXR 中生成一个黄金角花形网格，放在真桌上每帧精确旋转 137.5°。变体：让观众稍微改变角度，看花朵反向盘旋。

works.title: toki-
works.description: A 3D-printed lattice of intertwined figures spins while a thin line of projected light cuts through it, revealing a single walking or dancing figure that moves in space.
works.description_zh: 一个由相互缠绕的人形组成的 3D 打印网格在旋转，一道细细的投影光线穿过它，照出一个在空间中行走或舞蹈的人形。
works.idea_en: Light chooses the frame: an AR designer learns that a sliced reveal can turn a dense, unreadable object into a clear animated moment.
works.idea_zh: 光在挑选画面：AR 设计者可以学到，用切片式揭示能把一个密集难读的物体变成清晰的动画瞬间。
works.technique: Every frame of an animation is arranged radially in one printed object; as it rotates, a static projected light plane illuminates only one frame's slice at a time.
works.technique_zh: 动画的每一帧被径向排列在同一个打印物体中；它旋转时，一个静止的投影光面每次只照亮其中一帧的切片。
works.exercise_en: Build a ring of 24 frozen poses of a figure in AR, rotate it, and render only the pose crossing a virtual light plane. Twist: let the viewer move the light plane with their phone to scrub time.
works.exercise_zh: 在 AR 中用一个人物的 24 个定格姿势排成一个环并让它旋转，只渲染穿过虚拟光面的那个姿势。变体：让观众用手机移动光面来“拖动”时间。

works.title: Feral Fount
works.description: A spinning 3D zoetrope in which sculpted drops fall from a tap and transform into other forms, animated in real space by a synchronised strobe.
works.description_zh: 一个旋转的立体走马灯，雕塑的水滴从水龙头落下并变成别的形体，在同步频闪下于真实空间中动起来。
works.idea_en: Physical morphing in front of your eyes is more uncanny than screen animation; AR transformations of real objects can aim for the same dream logic.
works.idea_zh: 在眼前发生的实体变形比屏幕动画更诡异；AR 对真实物体的变形也可以追求同样的梦境逻辑。
works.technique: Dozens of sculpted stages of a transformation are mounted around a rotating armature; a strobe flashes once per stage so the eye fuses them into continuous motion.
works.technique_zh: 一个变形过程的几十个阶段被雕塑出来装在旋转支架上，频闪灯每到一个阶段闪一次，眼睛便把它们融合成连续的运动。
works.exercise_en: Model eight stages of a real object turning into something else, place them around a virtual turntable next to the real object, and flash one at a time. Twist: start the morph only when the viewer touches the real object.
works.exercise_zh: 为一个真实物体变成别的东西建模八个阶段，把它们排在该物体旁的虚拟转盘上，一次只闪现一个。变体：只有观众触摸真实物体时才开始变形。

works.title: Juggler
works.description: In a dark room a spinning sculpture comes alive under strobe light: objects arc through the air in a loop, mutating as they fly, like a juggling act in a dream.
works.description_zh: 在黑暗的房间里，一件旋转雕塑在频闪下活了过来：物件沿弧线在空中循环飞行，边飞边变形，像梦中的杂耍。
works.idea_en: Darkness plus a timed flash hides the mechanism and leaves only the illusion; AR benefits from similarly controlling what the viewer can and cannot see.
works.idea_zh: 黑暗加定时闪光隐藏了机械、只留下幻象；AR 同样受益于精心控制观众能看见什么、看不见什么。
works.technique: Sculpted keyframes spin on a large armature at a speed matched to the strobe frequency, so each flash reveals the next frame of the loop.
works.technique_zh: 雕塑关键帧装在大型支架上旋转，转速与频闪频率匹配，每次闪光揭示循环中的下一帧。
works.exercise_en: Make objects fly around the viewer in an arc in a dark room using HoloKit, each flashing into view once per second as a slightly different shape. Twist: sync the flash to the viewer's heartbeat or footsteps.
works.exercise_zh: 用 HoloKit 在暗室里让物体绕观众沿弧线飞行，每秒闪现一次，每次形状略有不同。变体：把闪光同步到观众的心跳或脚步。

works.title: Die Falle
works.description: A large stroboscopic sculpture shown in Science Gallery Dublin's ILLUSION exhibition, in which sculpted figures cycle through a looping, nightmarish transformation.
works.description_zh: 一件大型频闪雕塑，在都柏林科学美术馆的 ILLUSION 展中展出，雕塑人物循环经历一段梦魇般的变形。
works.idea_en: Showing an illusion in a science context invites people to explain what they see; AR can pair wonder with a reveal of how the trick works.
works.idea_zh: 在科学语境里展示幻象，会邀请人们去解释所见；AR 也可以把惊奇和“揭秘”搭配在一起。
works.technique: Persistence of vision: a rotating armature of sculpted stages is lit by brief flashes so each stage is seen only at one position (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 视觉暂留：装有各阶段雕塑的支架旋转，短暂闪光使每个阶段只在一个位置被看见（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Build a phone AR zoetrope with 12 models on a ring and add a toggle that switches between 'strobe' view and 'continuous' view. Twist: let viewers find the rotation speed that makes the animation lock in.
works.exercise_zh: 做一个手机 AR 走马灯，环上放 12 个模型，并加一个在“频闪”与“连续”视图之间切换的开关。变体：让观众自己找到使动画“锁定”的转速。

works.title: Blue Shirt
works.description: A 3D strobe animation shown at Wood Street Galleries in Pittsburgh in which a blue shirt and other everyday forms fold and transform in a continuous loop.
works.description_zh: 在匹兹堡 Wood Street Galleries 展出的立体频闪动画，一件蓝衬衫和其他日常形体在连续循环中折叠、变形。
works.idea_en: Everyday objects in impossible motion are the essence of good AR surprise: familiar enough to believe, strange enough to remember.
works.idea_zh: 日常物件做出不可能的动作，是好的 AR 惊喜的精髓：熟悉到让人相信，奇怪到让人记住。
works.technique: A motor-driven armature carries sculpted versions of the shirt at successive stages while a strobe tuned to the rotation freezes each stage into one fluid animation.
works.technique_zh: 电机驱动的支架载着衬衫在各阶段的雕塑版本，与转速匹配的频闪把每个阶段定格，融合成一段流畅的动画。
works.exercise_en: Scan a real shirt, rig it to fold itself in AR on a real chair, and render it at 8 fps like a strobe. Twist: let the folding speed up whenever someone laughs.
works.exercise_zh: 扫描一件真衬衫，在 AR 中让它在真实椅子上自己折叠，并以 8 帧/秒的频闪感渲染。变体：每当有人笑，折叠就加速。

works.title: Time Stratum II (時間層II)
works.description: Paper figures arranged on a rotating disc come alive as an animation because they are lit only by the flicker of video monitors, shown here at the Taro Okamoto Museum of Art.
works.description_zh: 排列在旋转圆盘上的纸人被只来自显示器闪烁的光照亮，于是活成了一段动画；视频拍摄于川崎市冈本太郎美术馆。
works.idea_en: Any light source with a rhythm can be a strobe; AR designers learn that timing, not hardware, is what creates animation.
works.idea_zh: 任何有节奏的光源都可以是频闪；AR 设计者可以学到，产生动画的是时序而不是硬件。
works.technique: Iwai synchronises the rotation of a zoetrope disc with the flicker of TV screens, so the screens act as a stroboscope that freezes each figure in turn (year approximate).
works.technique_zh: 岩井俊雄让走马灯圆盘的转速与电视屏幕的闪烁同步，屏幕于是成为逐个定格人形的频闪仪（年份为估计）。
works.exercise_en: Print a zoetrope disc, spin it on a turntable, and film it with a phone camera at a matched shutter speed; then add AR figures that match the disc's frames. Twist: use a screen flicker from another phone as the only light.
works.exercise_zh: 打印一张走马灯圆盘放在唱机上旋转，用快门速度匹配的手机拍摄，再加上与圆盘帧对应的 AR 人形。变体：只用另一部手机屏幕的闪烁作为光源。

works.title: Morphovision
works.description: A small model house spins rapidly while a projector scans it line by line with light, so the solid house appears to bend, melt and twist like rubber.
works.description_zh: 一座小模型房屋高速旋转，投影机用光一行一行扫描它，于是这座实心房子看起来像橡皮一样弯曲、融化、扭转。
works.idea_en: By controlling which slice of a real object is lit and when, you can deform reality itself; this is diminished and altered reality done with light.
works.idea_zh: 通过控制真实物体哪个切片、在何时被照亮，就能让现实本身变形；这是用光实现的减弱现实与改写现实。
